Repo: /opt/nxeon-v2, branch design/v2 (a design fork called "Nexion" of the Nxeon hosting platform). Read /opt/nxeon-v2/CLAUDE.md first — it has the operating rules for this tree (never run builds in /opt/nxeon, never pkill -f by pattern, etc). This session just built a light/dark theme system for the whole account dashboard (light mode is new; dark stays the default look). You are ONE of 4 parallel background agents fixing different, non-overlapping parts of this same light-mode pass. IMPORTANT COORDINATION RULE: do NOT run ./rebuild.sh, do NOT restart the nxeon-v2-web systemd service, and do NOT create any git commits. Just edit files and verify with `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit`. The orchestrating session will rebuild, screenshot-verify, and commit everything from all 4 agents together afterward, so a live screenshot against https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud will NOT reflect your edits until then (it's fine to use it to see the CURRENT/before-your-fix state, e.g. via the login flow in scripts/shot.mjs, just don't expect your own changes to show up there).

YOUR TASK: every account page has its own animated "aurora" backdrop — a full-page canvas drawing colored ribbons that drift and cross. They're drawn with `ctx.globalCompositeOperation = "lighter"` (or, for a couple of raster-image plates, CSS `mix-blend-mode: screen`), which only ever ADDS light on top of whatever's behind it. That looks great on the dark background these were designed for, but on white/light-page backgrounds it mathematically cannot produce color — it just washes everything toward white/grey ("this grey radial layer on top of the aurora streams" was the exact user complaint). Earlier in this session I band-aided this by adding a CSS class `.nx-mix-additive` that does `display:none !important` in light mode (see app/globals.css, search "nx-mix-additive") — this HIDES the backdrop in light mode rather than fixing it. The user has now explicitly said this is wrong and wants the auroras genuinely visible with real color in light mode too, not hidden. Your job is to do that properly.

THE FIX: each canvas needs to know the current theme and draw differently depending on it. Read the theme via `document.documentElement.getAttribute("data-theme") === "light"` — cheap enough to check once per animation frame (these already run a requestAnimationFrame loop), no need for a MutationObserver. For dark theme, keep EVERY existing value exactly as-is (composite mode "lighter", the existing hsla lightness values, same blur passes) — do not change dark mode's appearance at all. For light theme, branch to: `ctx.globalCompositeOperation = "source-over"` (normal alpha blending, so it actually paints color onto white) and LOWER each stroke's lightness value substantially (roughly deduct 25-30 percentage points from wherever the code currently uses ~60-80% lightness, landing around 35-50%, so the same hue reads as genuinely saturated color against white instead of near-white glow) — you'll likely also want to bump alpha somewhat since normal blending doesn't stack brightness the way additive does. Keep the same multi-pass structure (halo blur / body / hard core) each file already has; just parameterize composite-mode and color by theme inside it. Test your color choices by eye via a quick screenshot loop if you want (see scripts/shot.mjs for the login pattern — set `localStorage.setItem('nx-theme','light')` and `document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme','light')` before navigating, same trick used elsewhere this session) — you CAN rebuild/screenshot for your OWN iteration as long as you leave the service running when you're done and don't leave it broken; if you do rebuild to check your own work, that's your call, just be aware other agents are editing other files concurrently in the same tree so a build you trigger will include their in-progress edits too (harmless for typecheck/build purposes, just don't commit).

FILES TO FIX (confirmed via `grep -rl "globalCompositeOperation = \"lighter\"\|mix-blend-screen\|mix-blend-lighten" --include="*.tsx" components/nx`):
components/nx/StreamsBg.tsx, AuroraBg.tsx, ActivityAurora.tsx, BillingAurora.tsx, DomainsAurora.tsx, MailAurora.tsx, PartnerAurora.tsx, ServicesAurora.tsx, SettingsAurora.tsx, SslAurora.tsx, SupportAurora.tsx, TeamAurora.tsx, ToolsAurora.tsx, WhatsNewAurora.tsx.
These are almost all near-identical hand-written copies of the same ribbon-drawing technique (DomainsAurora.tsx is a good one to read first as a template — it's short and typical). Consider whether extracting one shared helper (e.g. a function that takes the ribbon array + canvas context + theme and does the draw) is cleaner than patching 14 near-duplicate files by hand — your call, but don't let it turn into a giant refactor that risks breaking each page's distinct look; each file currently has its OWN ribbon array (different hues/counts/speeds per page) which must be preserved.

DO NOT touch: components/nx/GlobeBg.tsx (already fixed this session with a different technique — it's a real photographic PNG, not a canvas, and now swaps blend mode via a `.nx-globe-arc` CSS class instead of hiding; leave it as-is), components/nx/BlobField.tsx (used only inside a card that's already forced dark regardless of theme via `.nx-dark-island`, so it never needs to change), components/nx/RegionGlobe.tsx (built earlier this session with its own light/dark handling — check it renders fine before assuming it needs work, don't touch unless you find a real bug), components/nx/RackHero.tsx and components/nx/Ribbons.tsx (grep hit these too but investigate what they actually are before deciding whether they're in scope — they may be a different pattern entirely).

Also fix components/nx/PlateBg.tsx: it has `Plate` objects with a `blend: "screen"|"lighten"` option (real PNG images, not canvases) that currently also get `nx-mix-additive` (hidden in light mode). Apply the SAME kind of fix as GlobeBg.tsx already got: switch these to normal blend mode + reduced opacity in light theme instead of hiding, via a new small CSS class (model it on `.nx-globe-arc` in app/globals.css). Once every affected canvas/image genuinely renders with real color in light mode, remove the light-mode `display:none` behavior from `.nx-mix-additive` in app/globals.css (or repurpose/rename it) and remove the `nx-mix-additive` className from every element that used it purely for this hide-in-light purpose — grep `nx-mix-additive` across the whole components/ tree to find every usage before deciding the class is safe to delete/change.

SECOND, SMALLER PART OF YOUR TASK: the user also said, of the /dashboard/refer page (component: components/nx/RewardsView.tsx): "fix the tags and cards and icons on referral page" — this was said in the same breath as "you removed the aurora streams", so once you've restored real color there, re-screenshot /dashboard/refer in light mode and look for any remaining low-contrast bits. Two known suspects, already spotted but maybe not fully fixed: (1) a cursive tagline "Better servers together" that uses a literal hardcoded color `text-[#8fd6ff]` (very pale ice-blue) — on a light page this is nearly invisible; consider swapping it to the `text-cyan` utility, which is already a theme-aware CSS custom property (`--color-cyan`) with a sensible light-theme value already defined in app/globals.css. (2) the small pill chips on each referral row reading "Awaiting first purchase" / "$X credited" (rendered via a `chip-q`/`chip-q-on` class pair — grep app/globals.css for `.chip-q`) — check these read clearly in light mode. Fix anything else you spot that's genuinely low-contrast or visually broken on that page in light mode, but don't do a wholesale redesign of RewardsView.tsx — it's mostly fine, just needs contrast/color fixes consistent with what's already been fixed elsewhere in this pass (theme tokens over literal hex, `.nx-dark-island` for anything that's a fixed dark hero/promo surface sitting on its own art rather than the page background).

CONSTRAINTS: only touch the files listed above (plus app/globals.css for the .nx-mix-additive changes and any new small CSS classes you add) and components/nx/RewardsView.tsx. Do not touch components/customer/vpspanel/v2/* (owned by a parallel VPS-resources-tab redesign task), components/nx/DeployView.tsx (owned by a parallel game-server-checkout task), or app/dashboard/services/page.tsx / components/customer/services/* (owned by a parallel My-Services task).

When done, write a clear summary: every file you changed, what the light-mode color values you chose were and why, and any files you decided NOT to touch and why (e.g. RegionGlobe already fine).

content.content: # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, **stop and ask the owner first.** ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. #!/bin/bash
# Rebuild and restart the v2 sandbox.
#
# The tree runs a PRODUCTION build (`npm start`), not the dev server: ~0.8 GB
# instead of ~4.5 GB, on a box whose spare memory is measured against fifteen
# customer VMs. The cost is that nothing hot-reloads — every change needs this.
#
# WHY IT STOPS THE SERVER FIRST. `next build` writes into `.next`, which the
# running server is reading from. Building underneath a live server replaces the
# manifests it has open and every route starts returning 500 — this has already
# happened once in this tree. Stop, build, start. Never build in place.
set -euo pipefail

cd /opt/nxeon-v2
LOG=/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log

# ── one build at a time ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two concurrent runs write the same `.next` and corrupt it — the exact failure
# this script exists to prevent, arrived at from a different direction. It was
# survivable only by accident: the build runs inside a transient scope, and
# systemd refuses a second scope of the same name, so run two and the LOSER
# fails loudly. Relying on that is relying on a side effect of a name. This
# takes a real lock and says plainly what happened.
exec 9>/tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock
if ! flock -n 9; then
  echo "==> another rebuild is already running (holding /tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock)."
  echo "    Wait for it to finish — starting a second one would corrupt .next."
  exit 1
fi

# ── skip the marketing site ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The redesign does not touch marketing, but it is ~137 of the ~195 route files
# and most of the 254 static pages, so it dominates a build we now run by hand
# after every change.
#
# Next excludes any folder whose name starts with `_` from routing, so renaming
# the route group is all it takes. This is a SANDBOX-ONLY, TEMPORARY rename: the
# trap puts it back whatever happens — including a failed build or a Ctrl-C — so
# git never sees it and nothing different is ever merged to prod.
#
# Set NX_FULL=1 to build the whole site (do this before any staging/prod pass,
# where marketing MUST be built and exercised).
MK="app/(marketing)"
MK_OFF="app/_marketing_skipped"
restore() { [ -d "$MK_OFF" ] && mv "$MK_OFF" "$MK"; }
trap restore EXIT INT TERM

if [ "${NX_FULL:-0}" != "1" ] && [ -d "$MK" ]; then
  echo "==> skipping the marketing site (NX_FULL=1 to include it)"
  mv "$MK" "$MK_OFF"
fi

echo "==> stopping the server (it reads .next; building under it breaks it)"
systemctl stop nxeon-v2-web

echo "==> building"
start=$(date +%s)
# Capped so a runaway build is killed rather than squeezing the customer VMs,
# and niced so it always yields to them.
if systemd-run --scope --quiet --unit=v2-rebuild \

## Summary

**New file:** `/opt/nxeon-v2/components/nx/auroraTheme.ts` — shared helper (`isLightTheme()`, `auroraComposite(isLight)`, `auroraStrandGradient(ctx, ribbon, w, isLight)`) used by all 13 hsla-gradient aurora canvases so the fix lives in one place instead of being hand-copied 13 times. Dark mode calling it with `isLight=false` reproduces the original expression exactly — dark mode's output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

**The fix, applied to every canvas:** each already runs a `requestAnimationFrame` loop, so I added one cheap `document.documentElement.getAttribute("data-theme") === "light"` read per frame. Dark keeps `globalCompositeOperation = "lighter"` and all original hsla lightness values. Light switches to `"source-over"` and drops each stop's lightness by exactly 28 points (62→34, 78→50, 64→36, 80→52, 66→38 — landing in the 34-52% band, genuinely saturated against white) with alpha multiplied ~1.7x (clamped to 1) since normal blending doesn't stack brightness across overlapping strokes the way additive does.

**Files changed:**
- `StreamsBg.tsx`, `AuroraBg.tsx`, `ActivityAurora.tsx`, `BillingAurora.tsx`, `DomainsAurora.tsx`, `MailAurora.tsx`, `PartnerAurora.tsx`, `ServicesAurora.tsx`, `SettingsAurora.tsx`, `SslAurora.tsx`, `SupportAurora.tsx`, `TeamAurora.tsx`, `ToolsAurora.tsx`, `WhatsNewAurora.tsx` — theme-branched per above. Removed the `nx-mix-additive` hide class from the 3 files that had it (StreamsBg, AuroraBg, DomainsAurora). `AuroraBg.tsx` predates the hsla helper (it uses a fixed 4-hex ramp, not a hue pair) so it got a parallel darker palette (`#14c5e4→#0a7a91`, `#2f7eef→#1a4fb0`, `#6f37d6→#5220a0`, `#d623e1→#a01aa8`) plus its own `source-over`/alpha branch instead of calling `auroraStrandGradient`. Also found and fixed a second, related bug in 11 of these files: their bottom-fade gradients used a literal `rgba(0,8,22,…)` dark-navy tint for their first two stops (only the last two stops were already theme-mixed) — this would have painted a dark wash over the now-colorful light-mode aurora, defeating the fix. Converted to `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-bg) N%, transparent)`, matching the pattern DomainsAurora already had.
- `PlateBg.tsx` — `screen`/`lighten` plates now get a new `nx-plate-additive` class (modeled on `GlobeBg`'s `nx-globe-arc`) instead of `nx-mix-additive`, so light mode swaps to normal blending at reduced opacity rather than hiding. (Currently no caller passes real plates with these blend modes — only `Shell.tsx`'s `<PlateBg seed={0} />` with no `plates` prop — so this is currently latent but now correct for when it is used.)
- `app/globals.css` — removed the `display:none` light-mode kill switch for `.nx-mix-additive` (confirmed via full-tree grep that nothing needs it anymore) and replaced that section's comment with an explanation of the real per-element fixes; added `.nx-plate-additive` light override; added `.chip-q`/`.chip-q-on` light-theme overrides (previously only dark hardcoded rgba, unreadable pale-cyan-on-navy on a white page).
- `RewardsView.tsx` — tagline `text-[#8fd6ff]` → `text-cyan`; eyebrow `text-[#8ea6cf]` → `text-magenta` (matches the eyebrow convention on Support/Partner/What's New); "Anything" stat `text-[#c9a2ff]` → `text-violet`; avatar initial `text-[#bcd8ff]` → `text-blue`; the positive-delta pill's `bg-[rgba(95,208,255,.13)] text-[#9fe4ff]` (pale-on-pale, invisible on white) → `text-cyan` with a `color-mix`-based cyan-tinted background.

**Not touched, with reasons:**
- `GlobeBg.tsx`, `BlobField.tsx` — as instructed, already correct/out of scope.
- `RegionGlobe.tsx` — verified it's a different technique: it paints its own opaque near-black radial "sphere body" via `source-over` *before* drawing land/cities additively on top of that self-contained dark base, so the additive layer never touches the live (light or dark) page background. No bug, left alone.
- `RackHero.tsx`, `Ribbons.tsx` — investigated; both have the identical `globalCompositeOperation = "lighter"` bug and both sit on the light page (Ribbons inside a plain `.card`, not `.nx-dark-island`) so they'd wash out the same way. They weren't on the assigned file list and the task's constraints section restricted me to the listed files, so I flagged this as a follow-up task (`task_7eddf874`) rather than editing them myself.
